We hope you find it useful. What is MEBO Wound Ointment? What are its active ingredients?View answerHide answer MEBO is the English abbreviation for Moist Exposed Burn Ointment and is the core pharmaceutical product for implementing Regenerative Medical Technology. The patented mechanism of MEBO Wound Ointment is based on beeswax and sesame oil. Beeswax provides the frame structure that holds sesame oil droplets containing all active constituents. The core active constituents are β-sitosterol, baicalin, and berberine: β-sitosterol has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; baicalin has anti-microbial, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, nerve-protective, and antioxidant properties; berberine has anti-microbial and anti-inflammatory properties. With what can MEBO Wound Ointment be used in combination therapy?View answerHide answer Skin Grafting: Such as conventional split-thickness skin grafting, microskin grafting, MEEK microskin grafting, and skin flap transplantation. MEBO Wound Ointment is applied before surgery for wound debridement and wound bed preparation, and after surgery to promote graft survival and epithelialization. Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (NPWT): MEBO Wound Ointment can be used alternately with NPWT. Other Topical Agents: MEBO Wound Ointment can be combined with other topical medications, such as antibiotics/antimicrobial agents and growth factors, applied sequentially or alternately according to the wound condition. CO2 Laser Therapy: MEBO Wound Ointment is applied immediately after fractional CO2 laser treatment to promote wound healing and reduce scar formation and hyperpigmentation. Physical Therapy: In the wound healing stage, MEBO Wound Ointment can be combined with red and/or blue light therapy to further prevent infection and accelerate wound healing. How often should the dressing be changed?View answerHide answer Acute Wounds: Dressing change is performed every 4 hours. The medication principles are “early application” (best applied within 4 hours post-injury) and “continuous application” (uninterrupted use throughout the treatment course). Chronic Wounds: Dressing change is performed once or twice daily. What are the indications for MEBO Wound Ointment?View answerHide answer Burn Wounds: First-, second-, and third-degree burns, as well as thermal, chemical, and electrical burns, etc. Chronic Wounds: Diabetic foot ulcers (Wagner grades 1–5, including wet, dry, and mixed gangrene); pressure injuries (stages I–IV and unstageable pressure ulcers); lower extremity vascular ulcers; radiation ulcers. Surgical Wounds: Post-perianal surgery (perianal abscess, hemorrhoids, anal fistula surgery, etc.); donor sites and recipient sites of skin grafts. Traumatic Wounds: Abrasions, lacerations, animal bites, etc. Medical Aesthetics: After fractional CO2 laser treatment; post-chemical peeling. Special Types of Wounds: Wounds caused by necrotizing fasciitis; wounds with osteonecrosis of bone and joint. Can MEBO Wound Ointment be used on infected wounds?View answerHide answer MEBO Wound Ointment is not only suitable for infected wounds but also possesses a clear anti-infective mechanism of action. Debridement serves as the foundation for anti-infection. The lipophilic components of MEBO Wound Ointment wrap around solid necrotic tissue under the action of body temperature and convert it from a solid to a liquid state through a series of chemical reactions, which are then actively expelled from the wound surface. During this process, bacteria and metabolites are removed together, thereby reducing bacterial colonization and disrupting biofilm structure, creating favorable conditions for anti-infection. At the same time, MEBO Wound Ointment can also induce morphological changes in bacteria, reducing their reproductive capacity and virulence. Studies have shown that when cultured in a MEBO Wound Ointment-containing medium, the morphology of Escherichia coli and Proteus vulgaris undergoes significant alteration, and bacterial virulence is markedly decreased. Physiological Moist Environment Maintains an optimal environment for cell regeneration, preventing wound bed desiccation and reducing pain. text: Regenerative Medicine | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/Regenerative Medicine Regenerative Medicine Regenerative Medicine Technology (RMT) represents a paradigm shift: instead of desiccating the wound, it creates an environment that mimics the natural physiological conditions of healthy skin. Core Technology From MEBT to Regenerative Medical Technology In the 1980s, Prof. Rongxiang Xu introduced Moist Exposed Burn Therapy (MEBT), with Moist Exposed Burn Ointment (MEBO) as its core therapeutic agent, transforming burn care in China. The breakthrough earned the State Technological Invention Award of China in 1988. Over the following decades, MEBT evolved into a complete regenerative platform — what is now recognised as Regenerative Medical Technology (RMT). What began as a clinical innovation for burns has become a reproducible regenerative system. The same principles now restore tissue in chronic, traumatic and surgical wounds, and dermatological diseases — offering patients worldwide a genuine alternative to conventional care. MEBT Era — Since 1980s RMT Era — Today MEBT EraMEBT Era — Since 1980sBurn Care, RedefinedMEBO Introduced by Prof. Rongxiang Xu, Disrupting Burn CareFirst New Drug Certificate for Traditional Chinese MedicineState Technology Invention Award of China, 1988 RMT EraRMT Era — TodayA Complete Regenerative PlatformCovers Burns Plus Chronic, Traumatic & Surgical Wounds, and DermatologyApplications in LATAM Countries and Access to 70+ CountriesOver 35+ Academic Associations / Societies in Cooperation with RMT One evolution — from MEBT to RMT, from burns to a complete regenerative platform. ACUTE VS CHRONIC WOUNDS The mechanisms behind RMT are not theoretical — they address real clinical challenges. Acute Wounds Caused by surgery, trauma or burns, acute wounds follow an orderly repair sequence and typically close within 2–4 weeks. Proper management keeps this cascade on track and helps prevent progression to a chronic state. Improper management of acute wounds can disrupt the normal healing cascade, subsequently progressing to chronic wounds. Chronic Wounds Chronic wounds stall in a prolonged inflammatory state and fail to close for more than 4 weeks — sometimes months or years. Most common: diabetic foot, venous leg and pressure ulcers. title: APEC 2023 Official Website Launches, with MEBO Group Listed as a Key Partner
desc: As APEC 2023's official website goes live, MEBO Group — a corporate partner and organizing committee member — launches the 'APEC 2023 Dialogue' interview series with the Marina Times and Entrepreneur to bring APEC closer to the public.
headings: APEC 2023 Official Website Launches, with MEBO International Listed as a Key Partner
text: APEC 2023 Official Website Launches, with MEBO Group Listed as a Key Partner | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC APEC 2023 Official Website Launches, with MEBO International Listed as a Key Partner July 8, 2023|Posted by: MEBO International APECSAN FRANCISCOAPEC DIALOGUEPARTNERSHIP The official website of APEC 2023 has launched, publishing information about the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting — with MEBO International listed as an important partner. APEC and its 21 member economies share a vision of an open, dynamic, resilient, and peaceful Asia-Pacific community by 2040, pursued through three drivers: trade and investment; innovation and digitalization; and strong, balanced, secure, sustainable, and inclusive growth. From November 12–18, 2023, the APEC Summit brings thought leaders and stakeholders together with political leaders around three policy priorities: building a resilient, interconnected region that promotes broad economic prosperity; creating an innovative environment for a sustainable future; and working toward an equitable and inclusive future. In 2023, MEBO International became an APEC corporate partner and organizing committee member, and MEBO Group Chairman Kevin Xu became Chair of the APEC working group at co-organizer Bay Area Council, launching a series of actions to help more people participate in APEC in different ways. MEBO International, together with the Marina Times and Entrepreneur, has officially launched the 'APEC 2023 Dialogue' project — an interview series bringing APEC closer to everyday life and fostering dialogue and cooperation across the Asia-Pacific in richer formats. MEBO International hopes the 'APEC 2023 Dialogue' series will provide a more accessible civic platform for exchange, generating new thinking and solutions to the problems we face today — not only in the Asia-Pacific but around the world. Partners from all sectors are welcome to join the interview project, connect, share their vision of APEC, and jointly advance the change we hope to see. headings: City of San Francisco Officially Announces Kevin Xu as APEC 2023 Host Committee Co-Chair
text: City of San Francisco Officially Announces Kevin Xu as APEC 2023 Host Committee Co-Chair | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC City of San Francisco Officially Announces Kevin Xu as APEC 2023 Host Committee Co-Chair September 22, 2023|Posted by: MEBO International APECSAN FRANCISCOHOST COMMITTEESPONSORSHIP On September 21, 2023, San Francisco Mayor London Breed publicly announced Kevin Xu as a leading sponsor of APEC 2023 and Co-Chair of the APEC 2023 Host Committee. The City of San Francisco recognized that Xu and MEBO International made tremendous contributions to the Host Committee, and that MEBO International's efforts strengthened the close ties between San Francisco and the Asia-Pacific region. In an official statement, the City noted that MEBO International generously donated US$1 million to the San Francisco Special Events Committee. As the first supporter of APEC 2023, the contribution not only paved the way for a successful summit but also demonstrated MEBO International's significant commitment to positive impact as a global business leader — reinforcing San Francisco's standing as a global city and deepening its ties with the Asia-Pacific in business development, cultural exchange, and community influence. Xu said San Francisco and its communities are full of opportunity and promise. As Co-Chair of the APEC 2023 Host Committee, he looks forward to fully leveraging the APEC platform, upholding APEC's mission, and focusing deeply on social responsibility and international relations. Hosting APEC is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for San Francisco, greatly strengthening connections between the Asia-Pacific, the Bay Area, the United States, and the world. The City's statement also noted Xu's conviction that APEC 2023 will engage younger generations in the organization's noble mission, and that San Francisco — with its open, inclusive communities and talented workforce — will continue driving the world forward. MEBO, founded by Dr. Rongxiang Xu in 1987 and headquartered in Los Angeles and China, is renowned for its Moist Exposed Burn Ointment and continues to grow under Kevin Xu's leadership as an international company dedicated to consumer health and well-being. The previous two host years (2008 and 2016) attracted more than US$9.4 billion in investment. text: U.S. State Department Releases 2023 APEC Outcomes Report, Bay Area Council Activities Listed as Key Results | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC U.S. State Department Releases 2023 APEC Outcomes Report, Bay Area Council Activities Listed as Key Results January 12, 2024|Posted by: MEBO International APECU.S. STATE DEPARTMENTBAY AREA COUNCILOUTCOMES According to the 2023 APEC outcomes report released by the U.S. State Department, important results were achieved around the host year's priorities of sustainability and inclusivity, digital innovation, and resilient and inclusive growth. Key deliverables include the Manoa Agenda for a sustainable and inclusive economy, the Pacific Agenda on digitalization, and the Bay Area Council agenda on resilient and inclusive growth. Kevin Xu — APEC Host Committee Chair, Bay Area Council director, Co-Chair of its International Committee, and head of its APEC working group — played a full coordinating role throughout, integrating forces from all sectors, gathering broad input, and pooling resources across business, academia, and government, enriching the content of APEC meetings and amplifying the influence of APEC 2023 across multiple platforms and formats. During APEC Week, civil society organizations and the San Francisco APEC Host Committee hosted nearly 30 public and stakeholder engagement initiatives, attended by more than 3,000 senior government officials and global business leaders — including the APEC Multi-Stakeholder Forum, the APEC University Leaders Forum, and APEC Study Centers conferences. title: Former APEC Host Committee Chair Kevin Xu Holds In-Depth Talks with Peru's APEC SOM Chair Carlos Vásquez
desc: At Peru's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Lima, Kevin Xu and 2024 APEC SOM Chair Carlos Vásquez discussed making APEC benefit broader communities — through a Silicon Valley forum, a Spanish-language magazine launch, regenerative medical training, and an APEC food week.
headings: Former APEC Host Committee Chair Kevin Xu Holds In-Depth Talks with Peru's APEC SOM Chair Carlos Vásquez
text: Former APEC Host Committee Chair Kevin Xu Holds In-Depth Talks with Peru's APEC SOM Chair Carlos Vásquez | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC Former APEC Host Committee Chair Kevin Xu Holds In-Depth Talks with Peru's APEC SOM Chair Carlos Vásquez June 23, 2024|Posted by: MEBO International APECPERUDIPLOMACYPREPARATION On June 21, 2024, Kevin Xu — former APEC Host Committee Chair and Chairman of MEBO Group — visited Peru's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Lima's historic center for a far-reaching dialogue with Carlos Vásquez Corrales, 2024 APEC SOM Chair, Director General for Asia and Oceania Affairs, and former Peruvian Ambassador to Singapore. Xu warmly praised Peru's efforts and contributions for the upcoming APEC week and stressed the importance of making APEC activities benefit broader populations. Drawing on the successful experience of APEC San Francisco 2023, he offered a series of constructive suggestions for enhancing the impact of the events. Vásquez showed great interest and shared the Peruvian government's vision of bringing tangible benefits to the public through the APEC gathering. Xu proposed activities spanning ideas, technology, and cultural exchange — a Silicon Valley forum, the launch of a mainstream magazine's first Spanish-language edition, regenerative medical technology training, and an APEC food week — to open more opportunities for public participation and benefit. Vásquez analyzed the proposals carefully and considered them of guiding significance for the preparations, stating that the Ministry's APEC affairs department would fully support the APEC projects carried out by MEBO Group to achieve effective resource integration and mutual benefit. Both sides expressed high expectations for the upcoming Peru APEC gathering as an important moment for regional cooperation and prosperity. The APEC SOM Chair plays a vital role in the APEC mechanism; Vásquez has served since October 15, 2023, with a term through December 31, 2024. The meeting between Xu and Vásquez injected new vitality and momentum into APEC's future development. Xu emphasized an unwavering commitment to advancing trade cooperation and development across the Asia-Pacific, noting Silicon Valley and the Bay Area's boundless potential for building trusted partnerships. The 2024 summit continued the dialogue among senior APEC representatives and Bay Area business leaders on the Bay Area innovation ecosystem, trade, investment, and global youth entrepreneurship. Initiated by MEBO International, the Action contributes to improving quality of life worldwide through technical training, disaster relief, burn treatment, and care for women and children's health. title: Preview: The 2024 APEC CEO Summit Agenda
desc: From November 13–15 in Lima, Peru's third time hosting APEC will bring together leaders from 21 economies and more than 1,200 executives — with MEBO Group CEO Kevin Xu joining the panel on aging populations, pandemics, and healthcare innovation.
headings: Preview: The 2024 APEC CEO Summit Agenda
text: Preview: The 2024 APEC CEO Summit Agenda | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC Preview: The 2024 APEC CEO Summit Agenda November 12, 2024|Posted by: MEBO International APECCEO SUMMITPERUPREVIEW The highly anticipated 2024 APEC CEO Summit opens November 13–15 in Lima. Peruvian outlet El Comercio has published an advance look at the multi-day agenda: this is Peru's third time hosting since joining APEC in 1998, gathering elites from the 21 member economies — which together account for nearly half of world trade and more than 62% of global GDP. Sixteen heads of state and representatives have confirmed attendance, including U.S. President Joe Biden and Chinese President Xi Jinping, alongside more than 1,200 business leaders from companies such as JPMorgan and TikTok. On November 14, Peruvian President Dina Boluarte hosts the official opening. A keynote on 'Business Strategy in the Age of Climate Change' features Unacem Group CEO Pedro Lerner, ExxonMobil chief climate scientist Vijay Swarup, and World Bank Managing Director Anna Bjerde. An AI panel exploring the technology's revolutionary potential in growth and governance includes Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Microsoft's Corporate VP of Data and AI Zia Mansour. The first day also looks at global financial prospects with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon in conversation with Bloomberg's Lisa Abramowicz, and at minerals for the energy transition with Chilean President Gabriel Boric. Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers the day's closing keynote. On November 15, TikTok CEO Shou Chew — on his first visit to Peru — gives an anticipated keynote, with Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau expected in dialogue. New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon addresses financial inclusion and the future of digital payments, followed by a major address from U.S. President Joe Biden in the afternoon. The summit also examines aging populations, pandemics, and paths of innovation: Thai Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra and MEBO International CEO Kevin Xu join the dialogue on the impact of demographic aging, lessons from COVID-19, and healthcare innovation initiatives. desc: At the Beijing stop of the APEC 2025 CEO Summit global roadshow 'Bridging Asia-Pacific Development Prospects', Kevin Xu joined a high-level roundtable and MEBO Group signed on as a global sponsor of the Gyeongju summit.
headings: MEBO Reopens the APEC 2025 Moment
text: MEBO Reopens the APEC 2025 Moment | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC MEBO Reopens the APEC 2025 Moment June 30, 2025|Posted by: MEBO International APECCEO SUMMITROADSHOWPARTNERSHIP On June 30, 2025, the global roadshow of the APEC 2025 CEO Summit — 'Bridging Asia-Pacific Development Prospects', the core prelude to the year's APEC series — officially launched, gathering business organization leaders and policy experts from across the Asia-Pacific. Attendees included Seong Woo Lee, Vice Chairman of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Secretary-General of the APEC CEO Summit Secretariat; Monica Hardy Whaley, President of the U.S. National Center for APEC; and Zhang Shaogang, ABAC member for China. Andrew Dy, General Manager of the Asia Business Forum, moderated the opening. Kevin Xu, former APEC Host Committee Chair and Chairman of MEBO Group, joined a high-level roundtable alongside senior leaders from finance, healthcare, new energy, and the broader health industry — including Catherine Simmons of Citibank and Monica He of Organon. Drawing on his deep involvement in APEC 2023 and 2024, Xu shared insights on how innovative cooperation models and sustainable business practices can genuinely 'bridge' the development needs of Asia-Pacific economies. He emphasized that the APEC platform's meaning goes far beyond trade and economics — its openness builds bridges for dialogue and co-created solutions, which is also the starting point of corporate social responsibility. As a mission-driven company, MEBO will continue building standardized medical networks to benefit all, serve refugees, and withstand disasters. desc: During UN General Assembly week in New York, Kevin Xu joined Panama's high-level roundtable 'Promoting Connectivity and Innovation for the Americas' — attended by President José Raúl Mulino — and proposed revitalizing Panama's humanitarian hub for disaster response across Latin America.
headings: Former APEC Host Committee Chair Kevin Xu Joins Panama Government Roundtable on Inter-American Connectivity and Innovation

headings: Silicon Valley Meets APEC Again: 2025 Forum to Be Held in Gyeongju, South Korea
text: Silicon Valley Meets APEC Again: 2025 Forum to Be Held in Gyeongju, South Korea | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC Silicon Valley Meets APEC Again: 2025 Forum to Be Held in Gyeongju, South Korea October 10, 2025|Posted by: MEBO International APECSILICON VALLEYAI GOVERNANCESOUTH KOREA As the official host venue of APEC 2025, Gyeongju, South Korea is welcoming a series of major events. Among them, the 'Silicon Valley Meets APEC 2025 Forum' will be held on October 16 at The K Hotel Gyeongju, an official APEC partner hotel. Co-hosted by the Bay Area Council and MEBO International, this annual event is an APEC-recognized flagship side event, continuing the deep Silicon Valley–APEC cooperation tradition begun at the 2023 San Francisco meeting. A defining feature of the forum is that it is not an isolated event but a year-long process of collective insight. In May 2025, the Sutter Health-hosted '2025 Bay Area–Silicon Valley Summit' gathered more than 300 leaders from government, business, academia, and nonprofits; in July, the Bay Area Council held preparatory discussions on AI policy, strategy, and regulation. The essence of these dialogues will be systematically distilled and released at the Gyeongju forum as a special report, 'AI Innovation and Regulation: A Silicon Valley Perspective'. Under the theme 'AI Impact: Shaping the Future', the 2025 forum focuses on two frontier areas: global AI governance, and the integration of digital technology into healthcare. Kevin Xu — Bay Area Council executive committee member and former APEC Host Committee Chair — and Seong Woo Lee, Vice Chairman of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, will deliver remarks. Xu noted that the platform aims to synchronize the Bay Area–Silicon Valley economic ecosystem with APEC economies, creating scalable and replicable paths for sustainable development. Highlights include a keynote by Microsoft's Director of Cybersecurity Policy John Hering on APEC's role in a global AI regulatory framework, the release of the special report by Sean Randolph of the Bay Area Council Economic Institute, and a panel on 'Healthcare × Digital Technology: Building a New Global Health Ecosystem' with representatives from MEBO Group, Deloitte, and Korea's Dong Wha Pharmaceutical. Since the inaugural 'APEC Meets Silicon Valley' forum aboard the historic Klamath ferry in 2023 — later cited by the U.S. State Department as a key outcome of the San Francisco APEC — and the 2024 Lima summit under the 'APEC for the People' framework, the forum has become a vital bridge between Silicon Valley's innovation energy and APEC's multilateral policy coordination. title: Kevin Xu's APEC Keynote: Building a People-Centered Digital Healthcare Future
desc: Speaking at the APEC 2025 CEO Summit in Gyeongju, MEBO Chairman Kevin Xu called for cross-economy collaboration to build a connected, inclusive, and sustainable digital healthcare ecosystem — and highlighted the new 'Silver Healing, Community Care' initiative with CGI.
headings: Kevin Xu's APEC Keynote: Building a People-Centered Digital Healthcare Future
text: Kevin Xu's APEC Keynote: Building a People-Centered Digital Healthcare Future | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC Kevin Xu's APEC Keynote: Building a People-Centered Digital Healthcare Future October 30, 2025|Posted by: MEBO International APECKEYNOTEDIGITAL HEALTHSOUTH KOREA On October 30, 2025, during the APEC 2025 CEO Summit, Kevin Xu, Chairman of MEBO Group, delivered an invited keynote titled 'Global Cooperation for Better Digital Healthcare'. Xu argued that the core of digital healthcare lies in the collection and aggregation of real-world data, and called for cross-economy collaboration to build a connected, inclusive, and sustainable dynamic digital healthcare ecosystem. 'Trustworthy, actionable, practice-derived data is the lifeline of digital healthcare,' Xu emphasized. True innovation begins in practice; only a digital ecosystem built on solid data can learn dynamically, adapt precisely, and optimize continuously. Drawing on MEBO's practice across the APEC region, Xu explained how the Group's wound care and regenerative medicine training integrates frontier technology with local medical experience — strengthening primary-care emergency capacity while gradually laying the groundwork for digital assessment and diagnosis. He highlighted how regenerative medical technology, pioneered by Professor Rongxiang Xu, offers accessible, effective solutions for the long-neglected field of wound management. Facing the diversity of APEC economies in resources, standards, and culture, Xu argued for balancing unified norms with local adaptation — citing the APEC 2023 burn prevention and treatment briefing, where AI and digital tools standardize care quality while respecting local conditions. He proposed three future priorities: innovative business models that pair growth with social responsibility; active responses to the health challenges of the climate crisis; and integrated global humanitarian platforms. Xu also highlighted 'Silver Healing, Community Care', a new initiative launched with the Clinton Global Initiative that aims to bring regenerative medical technology, standardized training, and multilateral cooperation to low- and middle-income communities, helping elderly populations access better wound care. 'We are not only healing wounds,' he concluded, 'we are building trust, strengthening resilience, and advancing shared prosperity.' Over three years — from San Francisco to Lima to Gyeongju — the former APEC Host Committee Chair has continuously contributed systematic thinking on Asia-Pacific economic cooperation and global health governance, and will keep extending the bridge of cooperation to broader fields. desc: Co-hosted by the Bay Area Council and MEBO Group, the 'Silicon Valley Meets APEC: Bay to Bay' forum in Hong Kong brought together business, technology, and policy leaders — alongside a CGI-MEBO healthcare innovation dinner attended by Chelsea Clinton.
headings: 4th APEC Silicon Valley Summit Concludes in Hong Kong, Empowering Asia-Pacific Collaboration
text: 4th APEC Silicon Valley Summit Concludes in Hong Kong, Empowering Asia-Pacific Collaboration | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/APEC 4th APEC Silicon Valley Summit Concludes in Hong Kong, Empowering Asia-Pacific Collaboration June 2, 2026|Posted by: MEBO International APECSILICON VALLEY SUMMITHONG KONG, CHINADIGITAL ECONOMY On June 1, 2026, the 'Silicon Valley Meets APEC: Bay to Bay' cooperation forum — the 4th APEC Silicon Valley Summit, co-hosted by the Bay Area Council and MEBO International — was successfully held at the University of Hong Kong's iCube Innovation Center. The forum gathered leading experts from business, technology innovation, higher education, policy research, and innovation ecosystems across Hong Kong and the Asia-Pacific, alongside officials from ABAC and PECC member economies, to discuss AI industrialization, the digital economy, and cross-regional collaborative innovation. Kevin Xu — Chair of the APEC 2023 Host Committee, Bay Area Council director, and Chairman of MEBO Group — delivered opening remarks, interpreting APEC's core value as a highly cohesive and effective multilateral platform. Since the San Francisco APEC Summit in 2023 established a standing dialogue between Silicon Valley and APEC, the two sides have built a stable, efficient exchange system. Landing in Hong Kong, this year's event built a two-way bridge between the San Francisco Bay Area and China's Greater Bay Area, connecting policy research institutions, top young talent, and private-sector players. Xu further noted that with China officially hosting APEC in 2026, the region faces new development opportunities. As an international free port and Asia-Pacific innovation hub, Hong Kong's hosting of the fourth 'Silicon Valley Meets APEC' dialogue opens a high-quality prelude to the full APEC 2026 series. Dr. Sean Randolph, Senior Director of the Bay Area Council Economic Institute, delivered a keynote on how AI is reshaping the global economic landscape, and panelists discussed building AI-driven economies and strengthening Hong Kong's position as an international innovation and technology hub. The same day, a healthcare innovation closed-door dinner co-hosted by the Clinton Global Initiative (CGI) and MEBO International was held at the Hong Kong Club, with Chelsea Clinton in attendance. In a fireside chat with veteran journalist Brian Calle, she explored Hong Kong's advantages as a top-tier Asian healthcare innovation hub, responses to global climate and public-health crises, the application and ethics of AI in medicine, and the role of youth leadership in global health. During the series, MEBO International and the NCAPEC Foundation signed a high-level strategic cooperation memorandum covering international public communication, cross-regional dialogue, cultural exchange, and sustainable development. The events were supported by HKU's Jockey Club Global Sustainability Institute, CGI, the Xu Peng Think Tank at the University of Chicago, Equitech Futures, and the Sacramento-China Office, among others. desc: Invited by Peru's APEC organizing committee COMEXPERU, a MEBO Group delegation visited ANIQUEM in Lima — Peru's only self-sustaining nonprofit offering free rehabilitation to burned children — to discuss donations, physician training, and child care programs.
headings: First Stop of APEC 2024 Activities: MEBO Group Visits ANIQUEM, Peru's Burned Children Rehabilitation Association
text: First Stop of APEC 2024 Activities: MEBO Group Visits ANIQUEM, Peru's Burned Children Rehabilitation Association | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/CSR First Stop of APEC 2024 Activities: MEBO Group Visits ANIQUEM, Peru's Burned Children Rehabilitation Association April 22, 2024|Posted by: MEBO International CSRPERUANIQUEMCHILDREN As the 2024 APEC series of activities prepared to open, MEBO Group traveled to Peru as an invited guest for an in-depth visit to ANIQUEM, the local burned children rehabilitation association. Last November during the APEC Summit, Host Committee Chair Kevin Xu held a meaningful dialogue with Peruvian President Dina Boluarte on how MEBO Group could play a greater role in the upcoming APEC activities and contribute more to the international community — ultimately reaching a 2024 APEC cooperation agreement with the President and APEC organizing committee COMEXPERU. COMEXPERU responded actively, preparing a series of related themed activities and sincerely inviting MEBO Group to visit local burn-related nonprofit organizations, aiming to share MEBO Group's rich resources and experience in burn treatment. On April 19, MEBO Group Vice President Liu Gang led an international department delegation to Lima, the host city of APEC 2024, visiting ANIQUEM. The two sides held in-depth exchanges on deepening public-welfare cooperation in response to APEC themes and the CGI commitment. ANIQUEM, Peru's only self-sustaining nonprofit NGO, has spent 25 years providing free comprehensive rehabilitation to child and adolescent burn survivors in poverty and extreme poverty — improving patients' quality of life while actively promoting prevention nationwide to reduce burn incidence. In the past year alone, ANIQUEM treated 2,859 patients, 50% of them children under five. ANIQUEM's head, Ms. Cecilia, and her medical team warmly welcomed MEBO International, presenting the association's history and achievements. The delegation toured the physical rehabilitation area, psychological guidance area, children's activity center, the workshop for self-made elastic bandages, the hydrotherapy area, and the burn pressure mask display area — each demonstrating meticulous care and professional technique. In the subsequent discussion, MEBO International expressed deep concern for local child patients and shared MEBO's founding story, the high compatibility of its products for burn patients, and the Group's outstanding record in public welfare and social responsibility. The two sides held lively discussions on donation implementation, physician technical training, and child care programs, agreeing to draft a proposal quickly and actively advance training and assistance activities — a meaningful visit that reflects MEBO's commitment as a mission-driven enterprise. title: MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Partnering with ANIQUEM to Build a Bridge of Care for Children
desc: MEBO Group and Peruvian nonprofit ANIQUEM signed a cooperation agreement to provide comprehensive rehabilitation — physical, occupational, and psychological therapy plus custom pressure garments — for children in poverty who have suffered severe burns.
headings: MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Partnering with ANIQUEM to Build a Bridge of Care for Children
text: MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Partnering with ANIQUEM to Build a Bridge of Care for Children | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/CSR MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Partnering with ANIQUEM to Build a Bridge of Care for Children October 16, 2024|Posted by: MEBO International CSRPERUCHILDRENBURN CARE As the APEC 2024 Summit approaches, MEBO Group — a key strategic partner of two consecutive APEC summits (2023 and 2024) — is demonstrating through concrete action Chairman Kevin Xu's firm commitment to the APEC ideals of cooperation, legacy, and sharing. On October 15, 2024, MEBO Group joined Peruvian nonprofit ANIQUEM to launch the Regenerative Life Action caring project for burned children. The initiative expresses deep humanitarian concern for burned children in Latin America and powerfully advances pediatric burn prevention and treatment systems across the APEC region. Since Xu successfully placed burn care on the APEC agenda in 2023, he has continued driving concrete action through regional cooperation and resource sharing, putting child burn injuries in the APEC region front and center. Xu returned to Peru after his October 3 APEC venue tour to attend the launch ceremony and deliver remarks. He noted that burn treatment may be only one corner of medicine, yet it carries great love and responsibility — affecting not only individual quality of life but the harmony and stability of families and society. He expressed hope that the APEC stage can bring all parties together to advance the innovation and popularization of burn treatment technology, creating a safer, healthier environment for children. Dr. Raúl Rodríguez Vilca, President and founder of ANIQUEM, shared the organization's remarkable achievements in burn prevention and treatment, emphasizing that the ANIQUEM-MEBO partnership brings hope for surgical correction of burn sequelae and comprehensive rehabilitation for children and adolescents living in poverty and extreme poverty. ANIQUEM is a nonprofit providing free comprehensive rehabilitation to child and adolescent burn survivors in poverty. APEC CEO Summit Executive Director Luciano Paredes praised the MEBO-ANIQUEM alliance as a model of enterprise-civil society cooperation toward shared goals — a vivid practice of APEC's commitment to 'prioritizing people's well-being and development' and an important step in regional health cooperation. At the ceremony, MEBO Group Vice President Liu Gang and Dr. Rodríguez Vilca signed the cooperation agreement: through physical therapy, occupational therapy, psychological support, and custom pressure garments, the two sides will provide all-round rehabilitation and build a culture of burn prevention for Peruvian families. At the event, the 'Little MEBO' panda toys prepared by MEBO Group were adored by the children, becoming messengers of friendship. The children painted freely on canvas, depicting their hopes for the future in brilliant colors. Most touchingly, Valentina created a colorful heart-shaped painting and presented it to Chairman Xu in gratitude — adding a warm highlight to this meaningful occasion. The Peru launch of the Regenerative Life Action children's burn project marks the grand opening of MEBO's APEC 2024 series of actions. title: The 21st ISBI Congress: Vibrant Mexico, an Academic Feast, and a Journey of Original Aspiration
desc: At the first in-person ISBI Congress since the pandemic, held in Guadalajara, MEBO Group — longtime platinum sponsor — drew global attention with a butterfly-inspired booth and held cooperation talks with ISBI leadership and UC Davis.
headings: The 21st ISBI Congress: Vibrant Mexico, an Academic Feast, and a Journey of Original Aspiration
text: The 21st ISBI Congress: Vibrant Mexico, an Academic Feast, and a Journey of Original Aspiration | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Global Programs The 21st ISBI Congress: Vibrant Mexico, an Academic Feast, and a Journey of Original Aspiration August 31, 2022|Posted by: MEBO International GLOBAL PROGRAMSISBIBURN CAREMEXICO From August 28 to September 1, the 21st Congress of the International Society for Burn Injuries (ISBI) was held at the Guadalajara Convention Center in Mexico. Guadalajara, Mexico's second-largest city, drew burn experts from around the world to discuss the future of burn treatment — the first ISBI congress to return to in-person format since the pandemic, showcasing the latest global research results, clinical treatment experience, and innovative technologies. At the opening ceremony, ISBI Secretary-General Professor Ariel Miranda delivered remarks, noting that the past two years had been extraordinarily difficult for the world, yet all those devoted to the cause of burn care can overcome hard times together. ISBI President Dr. Greenhalgh emphasized that ISBI, as a leading international burn treatment organization, should promote global cooperation to comprehensively raise treatment standards — and gave heartfelt thanks to contributors, highlighting that the consistent support of pharmaceutical companies is an indispensable part of ISBI's progress. As the platinum sponsor of this and many previous congresses, MEBO International has long been committed to growing with ISBI. MEBO Group Chairman Kevin Xu and Antonio Yung, Chief Representative of the Sacramento-China Office, attended the congress. Held by the International Society of Regenerative Medicine and Wound Repair (ISRMWR) in collaboration with the Rongxiang Xu, MD, Center for Regenerative Therapeutics at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) of Harvard Medical School, the symposium addresses the unmet needs of diabetic lower extremity management and explores the future of regenerative medical technology through global expert collaboration. The event was attended by more than 200 medical professionals from 17 countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Bulgaria, Greece, New Zealand, India, Ukraine, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and China. Dr. Aristidis Veves, Professor of Surgery at Harvard Medical School and Director of the Rongxiang Xu, MD, Center for Regenerative Therapeutics at BIDMC, delivered the opening speech, expressing hope that the symposium would catalyze new ideas among participants. Kevin Xu, President of ISRMWR and Co-Chair of the APEC 2023 Host Committee, emphasized that the symposium is not only a platform for academic exchange and knowledge sharing but also a unique opportunity to commemorate Professor Rongxiang Xu — and that achievements in regenerative medicine can be translated into greater impact at major international forums like APEC. Throughout the three-day symposium, medical professionals from around the world delivered talks on a diverse range of topics within the scope of the diabetic lower extremity. What makes the 2023 IDLES distinctive is its APEC session, where Dr. Tina Palmieri — Treasurer of the International Society for Burn Injuries and Past President of the American Burn Association — drew attention to the social and health problems caused by burns. Encouraging open-mindedness, she noted that regenerative medical technology, already supported by robust clinical evidence, holds great promise for the future. The 2023 IDLES was impactful in many ways: it not only illuminated new ways of treating the diabetic lower extremity but also generated ideas that could push the boundaries of regenerative medical technology. The prospects for medical research and cooperation among APEC economies have never been more promising. desc: At EWMA 2025 in Barcelona — nearly 6,000 wound management experts from over 90 countries — MEBO Group exhibited for the eighth consecutive year and co-hosted a regenerative medical technology symposium that also launched the European stop of the Regenerative Life Action global tour.

text: The 35th EWMA Conference Convenes in Barcelona | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Global Programs The 35th EWMA Conference Convenes in Barcelona March 28, 2025|Posted by: MEBO International GLOBAL PROGRAMSEWMAWOUND CARESPAIN From March 26–28, the 35th European Wound Management Association (EWMA) Conference was held at the Barcelona International Convention Centre, under the theme 'Breaking Boundaries and Barriers: Towards an Excellent Future in Wound Management'. The conference provided a platform for nearly 6,000 wound management experts from more than 90 countries, fostering multidisciplinary collaboration and broadening approaches to wound treatment. At the opening ceremony, EWMA President Kirsi Isoherranen thanked academic and commercial partners and introduced multiple ongoing academic projects. The conference featured more than 800 high-quality lectures showcasing frontier achievements in the wound field, and attracted nearly 200 leading pharmaceutical companies as exhibitors. Invited for the eighth consecutive year, MEBO International once again presented its core products — including the globally applied MEBO Moist Exposed Burn Ointment and wound dressings — alongside the latest clinical treatment protocols. The unique advantages of regenerative medical technology in wound treatment drew a steady stream of attendees to the booth to discuss and share treatment experience. Beyond the exhibition, regenerative medical technology made academic waves throughout the conference. On the first afternoon, the symposium 'Reshaping Wound Treatment: From Clinical Practice to Technological Innovation' was successfully held — a key activity advancing the Clinton Global Initiative commitment 'Mending Europe: Empowering the Establishment of a Regeneration Network'. Ziad Dalloul of Saudi Arabia's Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Group shared clinical management strategies for Marjolin's ulcer; Zhou Xiaoqian of Xi'an Ninth Hospital presented self-developed micro-particle skin slurry transplantation combined with regenerative medical technology for chronic wounds; and Nikki Valencia of the Philippines' Quirino Memorial Medical Center shared a latest systematic review comprehensively confirming the technology's efficacy, safety, pain relief, and infection prevention in burn treatment. The symposium also hosted a stop of the Regenerative Life Action global tour — its first in Europe. Since 2015, the Action has carried out diverse programs in technical training, disaster relief, burn treatment, and women and children's health. The next day featured lectures by Liu Yuedong of Liaoning University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Lee Chin Yen of Malaysia's Ampang Hospital, and Zhou Xiaoqian on anorectal postoperative management, pyoderma gangrenosum ulcers, and burns respectively. EWMA is one of Europe's most influential academic events, with growing global impact in the wound field. The next conference will be held in Bremen, Germany in May 2026. desc: Hosted by ISRMWR in Bali and co-organized with the Indonesian General Surgeons Society and the National Rongxiang Xu Foundation, IDLES 2025 gathered more than 300 experts from over 20 countries — featuring a special APEC Dialogue session.
headings: 2025 International Diabetic Lower Extremity Symposium: Global Experts Lead Innovation in Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care
text: 2025 International Diabetic Lower Extremity Symposium: Global Experts Lead Innovation in Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Global Programs 2025 International Diabetic Lower Extremity Symposium: Global Experts Lead Innovation in Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care October 23, 2025|Posted by: MEBO International GLOBAL PROGRAMSDIABETIC FOOTINDONESIASYMPOSIUM From October 22 to 23, 2025, the International Diabetic Lower Extremity Symposium (IDLES) — hosted by the International Society of Regenerative Medicine and Wound Repair and co-organized by the Indonesian General Surgeons Society and the National Rongxiang Xu Foundation — was successfully held in Bali, Indonesia. Focused on academic innovation in diabetic foot ulcer care, the symposium gathered more than 300 experts from over 20 countries, including China, the United States, the United Kingdom, Indonesia, and New Zealand. The symposium opened with a traditional Indonesian welcome dance. Opening speeches were delivered by Professor Aristidis Veves, President of IDLES 2025 and Director of the Rongxiang Xu, MD Center for Regenerative Therapeutics at Harvard Medical School; Professor Heri Setyanto, President of the Indonesian General Surgeons Society; and Dr. Li Li, Chair of the National Rongxiang Xu Foundation — recognizing the symposium's key role in promoting innovation in diabetic foot ulcer treatment and strengthening global academic collaboration. Over two days, the symposium held ten specialized sessions covering the full chain of diabetic foot ulcer diagnosis and treatment: treatment pathways, multidisciplinary collaboration, advanced therapeutic technologies, country-specific opportunities and challenges in wound care, and the latest clinical trial results. At the main venue, Professor Solomon Tesfaye analyzed 'Pathways to Amputation: Can Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy Be Reversed by Emerging Treatments?'; Professor Marc Schermerhorn detailed new diagnostic guidelines for peripheral arterial disease in diabetic foot ulcer; and Professor John Giurini focused on 'The Road to Limb Salvage: The Podiatrist's Role'. Professor Veves discussed new treatment directions grounded in pathophysiology, Professor Thanh Dinh analyzed surgical approaches, Professor Mark Wyers introduced minimally invasive revascularization options, and Professor Sammy Dowlatshahi systematically reviewed the reconstruction ladder, sparking lively discussion. During the critical phase of APEC 2025, the symposium specially held an APEC Dialogue session, where experts from China, New Zealand, and Indonesia presented national wound care practices, further strengthening regional medical exchange and cooperation. The symposium also introduced dedicated Indonesia and China sessions for the first time. In the Indonesia session, experts shared experience applying regenerative medical technology to wounds in tropical regions and promoted simplified protocols adapted for primary care; in the China session, experts presented results on integrative prevention and treatment of diabetic foot ulcer and limb-salvage strategies — offering a 'China solution' for global wound care. text: ISBI and ABA Join 'Mending Europe: Empowering the Establishment of a Regeneration Network' Initiative | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Global Programs ISBI and ABA Join 'Mending Europe: Empowering the Establishment of a Regeneration Network' Initiative September 19, 2022|Posted by: MEBO International GLOBAL PROGRAMSCGIEUROPEMEDICAL TRAINING The International Society for Burn Injuries (ISBI) and the American Burn Association (ABA) have joined the Clinton Global Initiative (CGI) commitment 'Mending Europe: Empowering the Establishment of a Regeneration Network', launched by former U.S. President Bill Clinton and Kevin Xu, Chairman of the Board of MEBO Group. ISBI and ABA will fulfill this initiative together with MEBO International and the International Society of Regenerative Medicine and Wound Repair (ISRMWR), delivering a series of training courses on burn prevention for both medical professionals and the public. Previously, MEBO International had provided regenerative medicine training to medical professionals across Asia, Africa, and Latin America. 'Mending Europe' aims to establish a regeneration network in Europe by providing medical training, medical supplies, and funding — helping local medical facilities and professionals master regenerative medicine techniques and gain the ability to deliver medical treatment during emergencies and disasters. Under this CGI commitment, MEBO International and ISRMWR have already provided online regenerative medicine training to more than 140 medical professionals from Bulgaria and Ukraine. Going forward, ISBI and ABA will cooperate with MEBO International to keep delivering more online and offline training across Europe. title: MEBO Chairman Kevin Xu Makes His First Official Visit to Panama
desc: On his first day in Panama, Kevin Xu met the Minister of Health and the President's medical adviser, lunched with the Chinese Ambassador, and visited the National Burn Care Association — laying the foundation for MEBO's public-welfare programs and market development in Latin America.
headings: MEBO Chairman Kevin Xu Makes His First Official Visit to Panama
text: MEBO Chairman Kevin Xu Makes His First Official Visit to Panama | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical MEBO Chairman Kevin Xu Makes His First Official Visit to Panama January 30, 2019|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALPANAMADIPLOMACYHUMANITARIAN On January 29, 2019, Kevin Xu, Chairman and President of MEBO Group, began his first official visit to Panama, consulting with senior Chinese and Panamanian officials on the international public-welfare programs MEBO undertakes in Panama and Latin America, as well as on investment, trade, and market development. On the first morning, accompanied by Ou Ruiqi, Chairman of Latin America Investment Advisory Group, Kevin Xu — together with International Market General Manager Liu Gang and Chairman's Assistant Tao Guoxin — met at the Ministry of Health with Minister Dr. Miguel Mayo and Presidential Medical Adviser Dr. Temístocles Díaz Strunz, both cabinet-level officials. Xu presented MEBO's 30-year history in regenerative medical technology and the UN 'Every Woman Every Child' program, seeking their advice on launching UN public-welfare projects and physician training in Panama. Both offered warm support, and the Minister immediately called the National Burn Care Association to arrange a visit that same afternoon. After the ministry meeting, the delegation was invited to lunch with Chinese Ambassador to Panama Wei Qiang. Xu introduced MEBO Group's history, its UN and Belt and Road public-welfare programs, and its intentions for investment and trade in Latin America; the Ambassador offered candid advice drawn from his many years of work in the region. That afternoon, as arranged by the Minister of Health, the delegation visited Panama's National Burn Care Association to learn about the treatment and aftercare of pediatric burns in the country, and invited the association to join future 'Every Woman Every Child' activities in Panama — an invitation warmly accepted. The first day proved highly productive. In the following days, Kevin Xu would hold further meetings with other ministries, the free trade zone, hospitals, and pharmaceutical companies, laying a solid foundation for MEBO's international public-welfare programs and market expansion across Latin America. desc: At the Clinton Foundation's CGI gathering, Hillary Clinton announced MEBO Group's new training commitment for Latin America and the Caribbean — 'Regenerative Wave: MEBT Training in Latin America' — and presented Chairman Kevin Xu with the commitment certificate.
headings: Regenerative Wave: MEBO International Launches a New Initiative for Latin America
text: Regenerative Wave: MEBO Group Launches a New Initiative for Latin America | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical Regenerative Wave: MEBO International Launches a New Initiative for Latin America June 5, 2019|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALCGILATIN AMERICAMEDICAL TRAINING On the morning of June 4, 2019 (U.S. Eastern Time), Kevin Xu, Chairman of MEBO Group, took the main stage at the Clinton Foundation's CGI gathering in the U.S. Virgin Islands to witness the official announcement of MEBO International's new training commitment in Latin America and the Caribbean: 'Regenerative Wave — MEBT Training in Latin America'. The initiative is a broad technical training program on regenerative medical technology for burns and wounds, launched by MEBO International in renewed partnership with the Clinton Foundation. Former U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Rodham Clinton introduced the new MEBO International project in detail and presented Kevin Xu with the commitment certificate on stage. Under the commitment, MEBO International will train 160 medical professionals in regenerative medical technology across Puerto Rico, Panama, Ecuador, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Chile, and Cuba, complemented by disaster preparedness and relief training. The earlier CGI commitment 'From Cities to Countryside: Regenerative Medical Technology Physician Training Program' had successfully trained 20,000 Chinese doctors — highly recognized by President Clinton and the Clinton Foundation — pioneering the global development of Chinese burn and wound regenerative technology. MEBO International has long been committed to cultivating regenerative medical experts who combine Eastern and Western medicine, and broad technical training is a vital form of the technology's internationalization. As initiator Kevin Xu noted, an international public-welfare commitment of this kind is not a simple path from here to there — it leverages international platforms to create a multiplier base for the global development of Chinese medical technology, exploring a Chinese path for public health philanthropy. He expressed the hope that more enterprises and organizations will take this road, using Chinese medical technology to confront world health challenges together. title: MEBO Group Restarts the Regenerative Wave in Latin America
desc: Honoring its 2019 Clinton Global Initiative commitment, MEBO Group and partner Difare relaunched the Regenerative Wave training program in Ecuador — reaching 400 healthcare professionals, far beyond the original goal of 160.
headings: MEBO International Restarts the Regenerative Wave in Latin America
text: MEBO Group Restarts the Regenerative Wave in Latin America | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical MEBO International Restarts the Regenerative Wave in Latin America September 12, 2022|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALCGIECUADORMEDICAL TRAINING In 2019, Kevin Xu, Chairman of MEBO Group, announced at the Clinton Foundation gathering that MEBO International would join the Clinton Foundation in delivering regenerative medical technology training across Latin America — the 'Regenerative Wave — MEBT Training in Latin America' program. Delayed by the pandemic, the commitment was renewed in 2022: together with its Latin American partner Difare, MEBO International officially restarted the Regenerative Wave in September, fulfilling the pledge to train 160 medical professionals in the region. The first session took place in Quito on September 6, with more than 50 local healthcare workers attending in person, connected live to a second venue in Cuenca with over 40 participants. The session was also streamed online, enabling 188 more professionals across Latin America to learn and interact in real time. The second session, held in Guayaquil on September 7, drew an even warmer response — local clinicians have applied regenerative medical technology longer and with a stronger foundation. A session planned for 80 attendees ultimately welcomed more than 100, forcing organizers to add seats on the spot. Participants came from public hospitals, private hospitals, and clinics, spanning burns, plastic surgery, endocrinology, gynecology, and pediatrics — evidence of the technology's broad local recognition. Local media followed the sessions closely with on-site interviews and coverage. The curriculum covered two themes: the global development of regenerative medical technology, and its current progress in Latin America. Xu Weiwei, Director of the Beijing Office of the International Society of Regenerative Medicine and Wound Repair, systematically presented the technology's history, patents, and mechanisms — providing a physiological moist environment, relieving pain, controlling inflammation, preventing infection, improving scars, liquefying necrotic tissue, and promoting in-situ skin regeneration — alongside recent global clinical research and complex case studies. Difare medical advisor Eduardo Pactong then explained the TIME principles of wound bed preparation and how regenerative medical technology addresses each step, emphasizing its outstanding safety profile and its importance for pregnant women, newborns, and children. He shared successful Latin American cases in burns, diabetic foot, and plastic surgery, and introduced mebo.education, the academic website for the latest global developments in the field. In a lively Q&A, the speakers fielded more than twenty questions — from effects on epithelial growth factor levels to combination with other therapies and standardized procedures. In 2019 we promised to train 160 Latin American healthcare workers; three years later, we have far exceeded that goal by training 400. MEBO International will continue expanding training programs across Latin America, bringing relief and benefit to more patients. title: Business and Academic Exchange in Ecuador: MEBO Group Sets Sail Again in Latin America
desc: During a week-long visit to Quito and Guayaquil, MEBO Group and its partner Difare reviewed market strategy, exchanged the latest clinical data on scar ointment, and witnessed regenerative medical technology helping diabetic foot patients avoid amputation.
headings: Business and Academic Exchange in Ecuador: MEBO International Sets Sail Again in Latin America
text: Business and Academic Exchange in Ecuador: MEBO Group Sets Sail Again in Latin America | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical Business and Academic Exchange in Ecuador: MEBO International Sets Sail Again in Latin America September 13, 2022|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALECUADORPARTNERSHIPCLINICAL VISIT From September 3 to 9, 2022, MEBO International traveled to Quito and Guayaquil, Ecuador, for a week of business visits and academic exchange. Back in 2010, MEBO International, together with long-term partner Gulf Pharmaceutical Industries (Julphar) and Ecuador's Difare Group, signed a strategic cooperation agreement. Over the following decade, MEBO Moist Exposed Burn Ointment (MEBO) and regenerative medical technology developed rapidly in Ecuador, with the ointment becoming the leading product in its category. The first stop was Difare's office center in Quito. Market development manager Jorge Duran analyzed how MEBO ointment could be developed more deeply under current policy; hospital channel manager Alex Frixone and product manager Katiuska Naranjo reviewed 2022 market share, sales, and competitive analysis; and medical director Dr. Iván Ludeña with medical advisor Dr. Eduardo Pactong presented the year's technical training activities for doctors, nurses, and pharmacists, plus next year's academic promotion plan. The two sides also preliminarily confirmed plans for a Regenerative Life Action under the UN 'Every Woman Every Child' China partnership network. On September 6, MEBO International and Difare's OTC team held a business and academic meeting on scar ointment, where MEBO technical director Xu Weiwei shared the latest global clinical data. On September 7 in Guayaquil, the delegation met Christian Konanz, General Manager of Difare's Dyvenpro S.A., agreeing that introducing new products is key to brand maintenance, with an initial import plan drafted. The following day, the team visited the clinic of Dr. Isabel Atocha, who has years of experience applying regenerative medical technology in diabetic foot care. She presented four patient cases — three of whom had been told elsewhere that amputation was necessary. After switching to regenerative medical technology, their wounds are healing well and amputation was avoided. The delegation also visited local pharmacies and met experienced local physicians, including Dr. Carlos Marquez, President of the Ecuadorian Burn Association, and Dr. Fernando Quintana, Head of Burns at Luis Vernaza Hospital. The trip concluded at Difare's 23,615 m² logistics center — built in 2020 with Austrian automation systems, processing 60,000 orders and two million products daily — where staff instantly located MEBO products among thousands of brands. Though brief, the week in Ecuador was highly productive. MEBO International and Difare took a major step forward together — and even in the farthest corners of Latin America, MEBO keeps moving toward new achievements. title: MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Latin America Forum Strengthens Regional Medical Cooperation
desc: Co-hosted by the International Society of Regenerative Medicine and Wound Repair and MEBO Group, the Lima forum brought together more than 150 healthcare professionals to advance regenerative wound care across Latin America.
headings: MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Latin America Forum Strengthens Regional Medical Cooperation
text: MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Latin America Forum Strengthens Regional Medical Cooperation | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical MEBO APEC 2024 in Action: Latin America Forum Strengthens Regional Medical Cooperation October 18, 2024|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALLATIN AMERICAPERUMEDICAL TRAINING On October 17, 2024, as a key part of MEBO's APEC 2024 series of actions, the International Society of Regenerative Medicine and Wound Repair successfully held the International Regenerative Medicine and Wound Symposium — Latin America Forum in Lima, Peru. Co-sponsored by MEBO Group and its Peruvian partner Discontinental, the forum launched a new wave of regenerative medicine in Latin America, drawing more than 150 medical professionals from public hospitals, private hospitals, and clinics across Lima. Kevin Xu, Chairman of MEBO Group and Chair of the APEC 2023 Host Committee, has noted that the APEC platform promotes the global dissemination and application of medical technology: through forums, seminars, and training programs, member economies can share advanced techniques and raise overall healthcare standards. The Lima forum put this vision into practice, aiming to deepen regional medical cooperation and expand the application of regenerative medical technology across Latin America. The agenda covered Latin American experience with regenerative medical technology and an APEC 2024 dialogue on pediatric wound management. Dr. Ariel Miranda, President-elect of the International Society for Burn Injuries, spoke highly of MEBO's technological value and corporate mission, while Jose Young, General Manager of Discontinental, highlighted MEBO's years of deep engagement in Peru and the added significance of the APEC dialogue segment. Dr. Carlos Marquez of Kennedy Alborada Hospital in Ecuador shared his experience treating pressure ulcers with regenerative medical technology, detailing treatment protocols and clinical advantages. Dr. Victor Coahila Carpio of Peru's Essalud Suarez Angamos Hospital presented successful cases in diabetic foot care, stressing the importance of early intervention and individualized treatment. In the APEC dialogue on pediatric wound management, Xu Weiwei, Director of the Society's China office, outlined the global incidence of pediatric wounds and explained how regenerative medical technology maps to the TIME principles of wound bed preparation. Dr. Miranda then shared his experience treating pediatric burns at the Guadalajara Children's Hospital in Mexico. Throughout 2024, MEBO Group has carried forward the impact that APEC created on burn care and disaster relief — launching the Regenerative Life Action for burned children in Lima and convening APEC burn-care dialogues. The Lima forum further energizes medical exchange across Latin America and offers a vivid example of APEC economies advancing healthcare together. Ariel Miranda's visit to the booth and in-depth discussion with the team highlighted the strong interest of Latin American medicine in innovative regenerative solutions. text: A New Chapter for Regenerative Medical Technology in Latin America: Diabetic Foot Symposium Successfully Held | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical A New Chapter for Regenerative Medical Technology in Latin America: Diabetic Foot Symposium Successfully Held May 8, 2025|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALDIABETIC FOOTPERUSYMPOSIUM Building upon the successful foundation laid during APEC Peru 2024, MEBO International — deeply committed to carrying forward the APEC ethos — officially launched the Latin America Regenerative Medical Technology Symposium series in 2025 in collaboration with its Peruvian partner Discontinental. On May 8, the third session of the series, the Diabetic Foot Symposium, was successfully held. The symposium shared diagnostic and treatment approaches for diabetic foot at various stages, comprehensively covering the pathophysiological basis, clinical diagnostic criteria, optimization of treatment plans, and the mechanism of action of regenerative medical technology. The first two sessions had already been successfully held: the first, on March 5, focused on 'Innovative Application of Regenerative Medical Technology in Wound Treatment'; the second, held on March 21, followed MEBO International's 2024 collaboration with Peruvian nonprofit ANIQUEM and was specially planned around pediatric burn treatment — the 'Application of Regenerative Medical Technology in Treating Deep Burns in Children'. These symposiums have not only provided new therapeutic insights for medical professionals in Latin America but have further propelled international exchange in regenerative medical technology. The core objective of the series is to stimulate collaboration within the region and actively contribute to raising treatment standards — while presenting new opportunities for global medical collaboration and showcasing the shared APEC vision of economies working together for progress in healthcare. title: MEBO Group at Hospitalar 2026 Brazil: Expanding Regenerative Medical Technology into Latin America
desc: MEBO Group debuted Regenerative Medical Technology at Hospitalar 2026 in São Paulo, drawing distributors and wound care professionals from eight Latin American countries.
headings: MEBO International at Hospitalar 2026 Brazil: Expanding Regenerative Medical Technology into Latin America
text: MEBO Group at Hospitalar 2026 Brazil: Expanding Regenerative Medical Technology into Latin America | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical MEBO International at Hospitalar 2026 Brazil: Expanding Regenerative Medical Technology into Latin America May 19, 2026|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALLATIN AMERICABRAZILWOUND CARE The 2026 Brazil International Medical Equipment Exhibition (Hospitalar) was held on May 19 in São Paulo, Brazil. As one of the most influential medical industry exhibitions in Latin America, Hospitalar brought together global institutions and companies across medical equipment, medical technology, and hospital management, providing a platform for international cooperation and market exchange. The MEBO International team showcased Regenerative Medical Technology (RMT) and related products for the first time in the Brazilian market, focusing on wound care applications, clinical cases, and product usage solutions — attracting strong interest from attending professionals. During the exhibition, pharmaceutical distributors from Brazil, Venezuela, Paraguay, Peru, Chile, the Dominican Republic, Bolivia, and Argentina expressed strong interest in regenerative life sciences and held discussions on product registration, market cooperation, and technology promotion. Local doctors, nurses, and wound care professionals engaged in extensive exchanges on RMT concepts and natural-ingredient wound care solutions, sparked by real case presentations and treatment outcomes. MEBO International also presented its Glymate premium health product series, focused on gastrointestinal health and blood glucose management, and reached a preliminary cooperation intention with a local pharmaceutical company. The two parties plan to initiate clinical trial projects on wound care and evaluate product application effects through real cases. MEBO also completed a preliminary feasibility assessment for Brazilian market access with local regulatory consultants. With a population of over 200 million, Brazil has significant needs in wound care and chronic wound management. Going forward, MEBO International will continue to promote RMT cooperation and exchange across Latin America, providing safe, effective, and accessible wound care solutions for local patients. title: MEBO Group Continues to Promote Regional Medical Exchanges, Focusing on Silver Healing
desc: The second 2026 session of the Latin America Regenerative Medical Technology Seminar series focused on regenerative treatment of elderly wounds, aligning with the 'Silver Healing' initiative co-launched with the Clinton Foundation.
headings: MEBO International Continues to Promote Regional Medical Exchanges, Focusing on Silver Healing
text: MEBO Group Continues to Promote Regional Medical Exchanges, Focusing on Silver Healing | MEBO Group Skip to main content Home Who We Are Regenerative Medicine Product Studies & Journals News Contact ES EN Contact Us Home/News/Medical MEBO International Continues to Promote Regional Medical Exchanges, Focusing on Silver Healing April 18, 2026|Posted by: MEBO International MEDICALSILVER HEALINGPERUELDERLY CARE In 2025, MEBO International joined hands with its Peruvian partner Discontinental to successfully launch the Latin America Regenerative Medical Technology Seminar program, which received widespread acclaim. In 2026, MEBO International is continuing the program with six seminars planned for the year — two of them closely aligned with the Silver Healing initiative jointly launched by MEBO International and the Clinton Foundation. The second seminar was held on April 18, 2026, focusing on the application of regenerative medical technology in the treatment of elderly wounds. It aligns closely with MEBO International's 'Silver Healing: Building an Equitable Community Care System for Chronic Wounds' initiative, integrating specialized technical training with grassroots community medical programs to support the accessibility of medical resources and health equity. The seminar specially invited Kenai Benítez Salgado, founder of Mexico's MediCalli primary care program, and Yu Ran, Head Nurse of the Wound Care Center at Nanyang Nanshi Hospital, to deliver special presentations — deeply integrating Silver Healing medical training with local community healthcare entrepreneurship projects and effectively enhancing the accessibility of primary care services. Aimed primarily at community healthcare workers from Peru's Padomi home care project, the seminar drew more than 80 in-person participants, plus online attendees from Argentina, Costa Rica, and other Latin American countries, to an enthusiastic response. The first two seminars have provided Latin American healthcare workers with new approaches to wound treatment and expanded the practical application of regenerative medical technology in community care. In the second half of the year, MEBO International will organize four more seminars, steadily advancing the rooting and growth of regenerative medicine in Latin America — bringing lasting, positive change to public health in the region and around the world.
